hero.title: An operator console, a much bigger shell, and providers that ship on their own.
hero.lede: The console is a TUI over the running broker, the sandboxed shell now picks up most of the bash you actually write, and providers ship from their own repositories. 0.11.1 repairs the container base and nothing else.

summary: The core rule is unchanged: models propose, the broker authorizes. The console just makes that boundary visible while you work.

highlights.title: A TUI over the broker that holds no authority of its own.
highlights.body: Run dekopon with no arguments and you get a TUI over the running broker: the selected agent, what it can actually do, and every script and result as they land. Its own execution leg stays empty.
points: Attested local development subjects are explicit and off by default
Every capability still reaches the separate broker
Render-time control stripping and field-level secret redaction

highlights.title: set -e, getopts, and PIPESTATUS now work.
highlights.body: The homemade interpreter picked up defensive options, compound pipelines, and richer parameter expansion. Still no host process behind any of it.
points: if, loops, case, groups, functions, and redirections compose
No host files, inherited environment, subprocesses, or ambient sockets

highlights.title: Providers now test and ship outside the core repo.
highlights.body: The public testkit runs a component against the real storage host. GitHub moved to its own repository, and a SQLite-compatible Turso provider now ships independently.
points: FakeBroker for end-to-end provider storage tests
GitHub component with nineteen narrow capabilities
Independent provider tags, assets, checksums, and provenance

path.title: The console watches; the broker still decides.
path.body: The console watches the same agent loop chat uses. It shows proposals and results. It links no policy, no credential store, no provider host.
path.ariaLabel: How one Dekopon console turn reaches the separate broker

changes.title: dekopon with no arguments opens a TUI over the live broker.
changes.body: It shows what the agent declares against what it was actually granted, then folds each turn’s scripts and broker calls. Watching can’t change the session, and the CLI keeps no local provider execution path.

changes.title: The defensive shell options models reach for now behave.
changes.body: Real errexit and nounset behavior, pipefail, getopts. Grouped pipeline stages and bounded in-memory redirection compose the way you’d expect.

changes.title: Storage-backed providers can test against the real host without standing up Cedar.
changes.body: dekopon-provider-sdk-testkit mints test authorization and drives the production StorageHost over a temporary root. It’s a development harness, not runtime authority.

changes.title: GitHub and SQL move at their own release cadence.
changes.body: The GitHub component left the core tree, walkthrough and all. Turso SQL adds SQLite-compatible durable storage through the storage interface that already existed. Core depends on neither.

changes.title: The console no longer borrows an identifier that looks externally authenticated.
changes.body: The new dev.<surface>.<name> subject family is admitted only when the broker explicitly enables development subjects. It still maps through owner-controlled identity and Cedar policy.

changes.title: The published image now matches the glibc required by the release binaries.
changes.body: Version 0.11.0’s image publish failed because the console binary named weak glibc 2.39 symbols while the Debian 12 runtime carried glibc 2.36. Version 0.11.1 moves the image to Debian 13; crate source is unchanged.

detailsIntro: None of this changes the path a proposal takes. The patch release changes only image compatibility.

telemetry.title: authority moved to the console, gateway, or model
telemetry.body: The console holds a model credential and watches one agent loop. Cedar, the credentials, and the audit all stay inside the separate broker.
telemetry.note: The current local deployment still treats one Unix UID as a trust domain. Dekopon remains pre-production.

packages.name: Homebrew
packages.body: The generated formula is verified against the current published archives and installs all four executables.

packages.name: crates.io
packages.body: All 25 public workspace crates, including the TUI and provider testkit, are published at the current application version.

packages.name: Container
packages.body: The Debian 13 distroless multi-architecture image carries all four executables.

installIntro: Homebrew and crates.io are current, as are the attested archives and the multi-architecture image. The latest published Helm chart is still 0.2.0, carrying application 0.10.0 — chart 0.2.1 exists in source and has not been published.

current: Interactive terminal console over one broker-authorized agent session
A broader bash-shaped language with no operating-system shell
Public provider SDK testkit backed by the real storage host
Twenty-five public crates published at the current application version
Independent GitHub, MediaWiki, Python, ripgrep, and Turso SQL provider releases
A published multi-architecture container image for the current release
next: Publish the chart update already prepared in source

Memory deletion and export workflows beyond on-demand recall
Further production hardening and incident-response automation

scopeIntro: The whole local path works today, from attestation through to telemetry. Stronger process isolation and an independent audit anchor don’t.
